factual_claims.claim: A study published in JMIR Mental Health found that large language models like OpenAI’s GPT-4o frequently generate fabricated or inaccurate bibliographic citations.
Across all six literature reviews generated by GPT-4o, nearly one-fifth of the citations (35 out of 176) were entirely fabricated.
Of the 141 citations that corresponded to real publications, almost half contained at least one error, such as an incorrect digital object identifier.
In total, nearly two-thirds of the references generated by GPT-4o were either invented or contained bibliographic mistakes.
For major depressive disorder, the most well-researched condition, only 6 percent of citations generated by GPT-4o were fabricated.
factual_claims.claim_label: Fabrication Rate for Major Depressive Disorder

factual_claims.claim: The citation fabrication rate rose to 28 percent for binge eating disorder and 29 percent for body dysmorphic disorder, topics less prominent in GPT-4o's training data.
factual_claims.claim_label: Fabrication Rate for Less Familiar Topics

factual_claims.claim: When prompted for a specialized review on digital interventions for binge eating disorder, GPT-4o had a 46 percent fabrication rate, compared to 17 percent for a general overview.
For body dysmorphic disorder, only 29 percent of real citations generated by GPT-4o were free of errors, indicating the lowest accuracy rate among the topics studied.
factual_claims.claim_label: Accuracy Rate for Body Dysmorphic Disorder
